# RFC-0007: Bounded loop in playbooks

> **Version:** 0.1.0 | **Status:** draft | **Phase:** spec
> **Owners:** @Will Eaton

---

## 1. Summary

### [RFC-0007:C-SCOPE] Scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0007c-scope"></a>

A playbook's graph is dispatched once. The one repetition it states is the revise loop of [RFC-0002:C-REVISE-LOOP](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-revise-loop), which runs again only on a failing verdict and for at most five rounds. An author who wants a set of tasks to run again while their own output says to has no construct for it, and unrolls the rounds at compile time: one copy of each task per round, each copy gated on a field the copy before it emitted. A two-task body unrolled 62 times is 124 declared tasks, the most a 128-task limit leaves room for, and compiles to 188 nodes and 249 edges once the route behind each gate is added. The round count comes from the task limit and not from the work, and every reader of the graph gets N copies of one body.

This RFC adds a loop. On its own the word means this construct here, and the revise loop and the scored loop are always named in full. A loop is a set of tasks, the body, that runs in rounds while a field one of them emits holds, up to a bound the source declares. The body's tasks are declared once and compile to one node each. A round is the unit the engine checks ceilings before, records, resumes from, and renders.

A loop keeps what [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-shape) promises. The node set, the edges, and the bound of every repetition are fixed at compile time, and only the number of rounds run varies. A loop uses the round model of [RFC-0002:C-REVISE-LOOP](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-revise-loop) (a row per round, one folded row per task, replay on resume) and leaves that clause as it is. Finalizing this RFC needs one edit to [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-shape), which says a revise loop is the only repetition the graph states.

---

## 2. Specification

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-SURFACE] Declaring a loop (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-surface"></a>

A playbook source MAY declare a loop by calling loop(body, again, rounds) and listing the value it returns in the tasks of workflow().

```python
turn = agent(name = "turn", prompt = prompt_file("turn.md"), session = "work", emits = ["summary"])
score = command(name = "score", run = "./score.sh", depends_on = [turn],
                emits = {"go": "boolean", "points": "integer"})
final = command(name = "final", run = "./final.sh", depends_on = [score])

workflow(type = "playbook", tasks = [
    loop(body = [turn, score], again = score.go, rounds = 60),
    final,
])
```

body is a list of tasks. again is the condition: a reference to a field that one body task declares in its emits under [RFC-0001:C-WORKFLOW](../rfc/RFC-0001.md#rfc-0001c-workflow). A bare reference names a field typed boolean and holds when the field is true. A reference followed by any_of(...) names a field typed as a list of labels and holds when the field is one of the labels listed. The body task whose field the condition reads is the deciding task. rounds is the most rounds the loop may run, the first included, and has no default.

The compiler MUST reject a loop whose body is empty or names one task twice. It MUST reject an again that is absent, that is not a field reference, that names a task outside the body, that names a field the task does not declare, that names a field typed as anything other than boolean or a list of labels, that lists a label the field does not declare, or that uses otherwise(). It MUST reject a rounds that is absent or outside 1 to 256 inclusive. The upper bound is the engine's, and a source MUST NOT be able to raise it. The compiler MUST reject any other argument to loop().

Listing a loop in tasks lists its body's tasks, and each keeps the name the source gave it. The compiler MUST reject a task listed both through a loop and on its own, and MUST reject a loop that the source constructs and does not list. The engine MUST reject a loop in every workflow type other than "playbook".

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-BODY] What a body may hold (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-body"></a>

The engine MUST reject a loop in which any body task is anything other than an agent, command, or evaluate task, or maps over a list. The engine MUST reject a body that omits a task lying on a dependency path between two body tasks: a round re-runs the body, and a task between two body tasks outside it would read a result a later round replaces.

The engine MUST reject a task that is in two loops. It MUST reject a task that is in a loop's body and is also a reviewer or a target under [RFC-0002:C-REVISE-LOOP](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-revise-loop). Loops do not nest, do not chain, and do not contain a revise loop. The engine MUST reject a body that holds both a main-graph task and an epilogue task.

The engine MUST reject a body task whose when reads a field of another body task, because the route that answers that when would lie between two body tasks and a route cannot be in a body. A body task's when MAY read an answer produced outside the body.

These checks apply to every plan the engine admits, whatever produced it.

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-SHAPE] What a loop compiles to (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-shape"></a>

The compiled graph MUST contain each body task exactly once, under the name the source gave it, whatever rounds declares. A loop MUST NOT add a task, a route, or an edge to the compiled graph. The condition is read from the deciding task's output and MUST NOT compile to a route.

Each body task MUST count once against the plan's task limit. The loop, its condition, and its rounds MUST NOT count against it.

The admitted-plan event MUST carry, on the deciding task, the names of the body's tasks in dispatch order under "loop", the condition under "again", and the bound under "loop_rounds". The condition MUST be written in the form the event carries a task's when, with the deciding task and field in place of the route and question, so the example in [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-SURFACE](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-loop-surface) carries "score.go in yes". The event MUST carry an empty list, an empty string, and zero under those keys for every other task, so a reader that predates loops reads every plan without one. A deciding task MUST carry an empty value under "revise" and zero under "max_rounds", as [RFC-0002:C-REVISE-LOOP](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-revise-loop) requires of a task that is not a reviewer.

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-ROUNDS] Running rounds (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-rounds"></a>

The engine MUST NOT dispatch a loop's first round until every dependency outside the body of every body task has settled, and MUST NOT dispatch a task outside the body that depends on a body task until every body task has settled under its own name. Where any body task cannot run on the substrate, the engine MUST dispatch the body's tasks once as tasks outside any loop and MUST settle each one that cannot run as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-CAPS](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-caps) requires.

A round dispatches the body's tasks one at a time in dependency order, each under its own join and when against this round's results for the body and the settled results outside it. A body task whose join those results do not satisfy MUST settle blocked for that round, and one whose when excludes it MUST settle not taken for that round, as any task would. A retry of a transport failure belongs to the round its first attempt was in.

The condition is checked after a round, never before the first. Once a round has settled, the engine MUST begin another round when all four of these hold, and MUST NOT begin one when any of them does not. First, the deciding task settled passing in that round and the field in its output satisfies the condition. Second, every other body task settled passing or not taken in that round. Third, fewer than rounds rounds have run. Fourth, no ceiling is exhausted under [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-BUDGET](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-loop-budget) and dispatch has not stopped for any other reason.

A loop that ends because its rounds are spent while the condition still holds is not a failure. The engine MUST NOT change a body task's status, the run's verdict, or the shutdown outcome on that ground. An early completion the engine accepts from a body task under [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-LANE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-lane) MUST end the loop with that round.

Every round settles its work as any task does. A body task's workspace changes MUST be committed to the run's git memory when its round settles passing and MUST be discarded otherwise, as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-LANE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-lane) requires, so a later round runs on top of every earlier passing round. A round's captured file set MUST replace the set its task published in an earlier round under the rules of [RFC-0002:C-TASK-FILES](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-task-files) and [RFC-0002:C-SETTLED-JOIN](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-settled-join). A body task that declares a session MUST resume that session in every round.

Once the loop has ended, each body task settles as its last round did, and a dependent of a body task MUST read that round's output and captured files.

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-INPUTS] What a round reads (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-inputs"></a>

In every round the engine MUST give each body task the reserved input "loop". It MUST carry under "round" the number of the round about to run, counted from 1, under "max_rounds" the declared bound, and under "previous" an object. In the first round "previous" MUST be empty. In every later round "previous" MUST hold one entry for each body task that settled passing in the round before, under that task's name, holding that round's JSON output. It MUST NOT hold an entry for a body task that settled not taken in the round before, and MUST NOT hold output from any earlier round.

```json
{"round": 3, "max_rounds": 60,
 "previous": {"turn": {"summary": "tightened the parser"}, "score": {"go": true, "points": 41}}}
```

The engine MUST NOT give "loop" to a task outside the body. The name is reserved for body tasks only: the engine MUST reject a body task that declares a dependency named "loop", and MUST NOT reject that name on any other task.

Within a round, a body task reads another body task's output and captured files from the same round through its dependency on that task, under the rules that apply outside a loop. The engine MUST NOT give a body task an earlier round's result through a dependency.

A file a passing round wrote is in the workspace for later rounds because [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-LANE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-lane) commits it. It is not staged as an input.

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-BUDGET] Ceilings (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-budget"></a>

A loop can spend, in the sense of [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-BUDGET](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-budget), when any task of its body can. The engine MUST check the cost and wall-clock ceilings before every round after the first, and before every dispatch within a round that the task's join and when would allow. An exhausted ceiling MUST end the loop and halt the run as it would halt any dispatch. Within a round, a body task not dispatched because of a ceiling MUST settle blocked for that round, naming the ceiling. A loop ended by a ceiling between rounds MUST leave each body task settled as its last round did. Every round's spend MUST count against the cost ceiling as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-BUDGET](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-budget) counts any task's.

A loop has no ceiling of its own, and rounds is not a budget. The engine MUST NOT refuse to begin a round on the ground that the rounds still allowed could exceed a ceiling. A task's own per-attempt limit under [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-BUDGET](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-budget) applies to each attempt of each round separately.

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-RECORD] Session rows (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-record"></a>

Each round of each body task MUST produce one session row named after the task followed by "[round-N]", written as that round settles and carrying that round's status, output, note, and spend. N counts from 1 and MUST have no gaps. A first round that dispatched no body task MUST produce no round rows.

Once the loop has ended, each body task MUST produce one row under its own name carrying its last round's status, output, note, blocked reason, and transport cause, and the sum of every round's spend. A round row MUST NOT affect the verdict or halt the run. The rows under the tasks' own names do, exactly as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-LANE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-lane) states for any task.

A reader MUST be able to tell why a loop ended from the session log alone. The deciding task's last round row carries the field the condition read, the count of round rows gives the rounds run, and the shutdown event names an exhausted ceiling.

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-RESUME] Resumption and rerun (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-resume"></a>

A resumed run MUST treat a folded round row as terminal for that round of that task and MUST NOT dispatch that round of that task again. Where the interruption cut a round, the engine MUST dispatch only the body tasks that have no row for that round, in dependency order, against the folded results of that round. It MUST NOT restart the round or the loop.

The engine MUST decide whether to begin the next round from the folded round rows by the rule in [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-ROUNDS](../rfc/RFC-0007.md#rfc-0007c-loop-rounds). That decision MUST depend only on the admitted plan, the round rows, and the ceilings, so a resumed run begins exactly the rounds the interrupted run would have. Folded rounds count toward rounds. Their spend and elapsed time count against the ceilings as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-RESUME](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-resume) requires.

The input "loop" a resumed round receives MUST be the one an uninterrupted run would have given it, with "previous" built from the folded rows. A resumed run MUST reconstruct its workspace as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-RESUME](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-resume) requires, taking for each body task the declared files of its latest round that settled passing. Where a body task's own-name row is folded, the loop has ended, and the engine MUST NOT dispatch any round of it.

Where a rerun under [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-RERUN](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-rerun) reruns a body task, the engine MUST rerun every task of that body from round 1 and MUST NOT reuse a round row of the parent.

### [RFC-0007:C-LOOP-GRAPH] Graph views (Normative) <a id="rfc-0007c-loop-graph"></a>

Four views draw a playbook's graph: the mermaid source crucible plan show prints for a compiled plan, the run graph crux graph prints as a table and as mermaid, and the graph the desktop app draws. Each MUST show a body task as one node, whatever number of rounds ran.

Each of the three flowcharts MUST enclose the nodes of a loop's body, and no other node, in one subgraph titled "loop". It MUST draw one dotted edge from the deciding task's node to the node of the first task named under "loop" in the admitted-plan event, and MUST draw that edge where the two are the same task. It MUST NOT draw any other edge for the loop. Edges between body tasks, and between a body task and a task outside the body, are drawn as they are outside a loop.

That edge's label MUST name the field the condition reads and the values it holds on, in the form the view labels an edge that a when on that field gates, followed by the bound. The bound is written as in "≤60" in the compiled-plan view, and in a run view before any round has begun. After that a run view writes the number of rounds begun over the bound, as in "12/60".

```text
flowchart TD
  subgraph loop0["loop"]
    turn(["turn"])
    score["score"]
  end
  turn --> score
  score -.->|go: yes 12/60| turn
  score --> final["final"]
```

In the two run flowcharts each body task's node MUST also show a round counter in the form a revised task's node uses in the desktop app: the round in flight, or the last round settled when none is in flight, over the bound, as in "r12/60". Before any round has run, the node MUST show the bound alone. The node's status MUST be the status of the round the counter names until the task's own-name row is written, and that row's status after.

The table crux graph prints MUST mark each body task's row as part of the loop, MUST show the loop's condition and bound, and MUST show each body task's round counter.

The desktop app MUST list a body task's rounds under that task, each with its status and spend, as it lists the rounds of a revised task.

A reader that predates loops draws the body's tasks as ordinary nodes and their round rows as it draws a mapped task's instances. That is the accepted behavior for such a reader.

## 3. Rationale

### [RFC-0007:C-ALTERNATIVES] Alternatives considered (Informative) <a id="rfc-0007c-alternatives"></a>

Five designs were weighed. The first two are the ones that need no new construct.

Keep unrolling and fold the copies in the renderer. The engine does not change, and each round stays a task of its own that a rerun can select. It loses on everything except the picture. The round count stays tied to the task limit, and raising the limit grows the admitted plan, the compile cost, and the embedded prompt total by one copy of the body per round. A loop that stops at round 3 of 62 still writes a not-taken row for every task and route of the other 59 rounds. Every reader of the graph (crux graph, the desktop app, the run export, a report's task list) would have to infer the same loop from task names, and a pack that names its copies another way is not folded. Launch settings, definition digests, and rerun selection all stay per copy. Rejected.

Lift the revise ceiling and make revise run on a condition. This adds no new name to the DSL. It loses because a revise round and a loop round mean opposite things. A revise loop continues on a failing verdict, discards the failing round's work, hands the verdict back as "revision", and settles the reviewer failed when the rounds are spent. A loop continues on a passing round, commits it, and ends without a failure when the rounds are spent. To continue on the existing rules an author would have to fail the scoring task every round, which discards the work the round did and fails the run at the bound. To continue without failing, every rule of [RFC-0002:C-REVISE-LOOP](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-revise-loop) would fork on a mode: commit or discard, "revision" or not, pass or fail at the bound. The ceiling of five is also deliberate for rework, where each round re-pays for the same output. Rejected as a surface. Accepted as machinery: a loop uses the same round rows, the same folded row per task, the same checks between rounds, and the same replay on resume.

A reserved output field in place of a declared reference, the way "complete" ends a run. The last body task would return "again": true. It avoids naming a field in the source, but the condition is then invisible in the compiled graph, untyped, and unchecked at compile time. Rejected.

Loop inside one task, as [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-SHAPE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-shape) advises for polling. It is the right answer when the rounds do not deserve their own budget check, row, commit, or resume point. It is the wrong one when a round pairs an agent turn with a check the engine runs separately, which one task cannot hold. Unchanged and still recommended where it fits.

Reuse the scored loop. Its iteration is propose, apply, measure, decide against a judge and a baseline, with keep or discard and operator parking between iterations. A playbook has no judge under [RFC-0002:C-PLAYBOOK-LANE](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-playbook-lane), and a loop round keeps no best candidate and discards nothing on a score. The two share the session log and the task rows and nothing of the driver. Rejected.

On the name. The construct is called loop because that is the established name for the pattern it serves: an agent turn run again and again on the same prompt until a check says stop, widely known as a Ralph loop. repeat was the other candidate and was dropped so the DSL matches the term authors already use. while is a reserved word in Starlark, so the condition is again.

### [RFC-0007:C-OUT-OF-SCOPE] Out of scope (Informative) <a id="rfc-0007c-out-of-scope"></a>

This RFC does not cover the following. Each can be added later without changing a clause above.

A loop inside a loop, a revise loop inside a loop, and a mapped task inside a body. A route inside a body, which includes a condition a decision model or a person answers. A body whose tasks run concurrently, and rounds that run concurrently. A rerun that starts from a chosen round. A launch setting that lowers rounds for one launch. A cost or time ceiling scoped to one loop, and a loop that ends itself cleanly as a run ceiling approaches. An input that carries more than the previous round. Any change to [RFC-0002:C-REVISE-LOOP](../rfc/RFC-0002.md#rfc-0002c-revise-loop), its ceiling of five rounds, or the scored loop.
